guard_policy.input_contract: Exact JSON authorization object, exact binding hash and payload descriptor, exact helper hash/marker, exact owner-only certificate/key/server-CA files and exact output paths.
guard_policy.binding_policy: The binding carries event_authorized=false; only the exact separate authorization object may set event_authorized=true. The binding payload is exactly topic V, transaction type V, VehicleName string and single-wrapper-created-at-ms timestamp source.
guard_policy.path_policy: All inputs are absolute, non-symlink regular files owned by the invoking user with one hard link and no group/world access. Certificate, key and server-CA paths must be distinct.
guard_policy.timestamp_policy: After every authorization/profile/hash/path check and an existing-guard check, call the supplied CLOCK_REALTIME Unix-ms function exactly once. Reject zero, negative or expired values.
guard_policy.guard_policy: Immediately after that one timestamp read, create the guard with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL and mode 0600. EEXIST is final already-consumed state.
guard_policy.spawn_policy: Pass the identical timestamp and exact argv order to one subprocess.run call with shell=false, stdin=DEVNULL, captured output and a maximum 30-second authorization timeout. No retry or replay path exists.
guard_policy.result_policy: Record completed, failed_no_retry or timed_out_no_retry once. Persist result through a same-directory 0600 temporary file, fsync, hard-link publication and temporary-file removal; never overwrite an existing result.
guard_policy.redaction_policy: Guard and result records contain hashes, transaction and timestamp metadata but not the sealed VIN, private key bytes, certificate bytes or private credential values.
